body:
## Problem Statement

Die heutige Eventaufgabe ist eine Checkbox mit Titel, optionalem Datum und Freitext-Verantwortlichem. Mitarbeitende können damit offene Arbeit, Zuständigkeit, Terminlage und Verlauf nicht verlässlich über Eventgrenzen hinweg steuern. Die globale Aufgabenansicht basiert auf lokal geladenen Eventdaten und ist weder vollständig noch für n8n robust abfragbar. Wiederkehrende Events brauchen Standards, ohne operative Daten vergangener Jahre zu kopieren oder zu verändern.

## Solution

t2w-base erhält ein integriertes Projektmanagement innerhalb des bestehenden Event-Workspace und der bestehenden globalen Aufgabenansicht. Ein Event ist der operative Projektcontainer; eine benannte Eventserie besitzt künftig versionierte Aufgabenserien. Der MVP liefert serverseitig abfragbare, versionssichere Eventaufgaben mit vier Arbeitsstatus, Owner, administrierbarer Gruppe, Priorität, Frist, nächstem Schritt und einem sichtbaren Aktivitätslog. n8n erhält einen eingeschränkten lesenden Zugriff; das PM-Modul versendet keine Nachrichten.

## User Stories

1. As an active employee, I want to create an Event task with a title, so that I can capture work immediately.
2. As an active employee, I want to start a task only after assigning an active owner, group, and next step, so that active work is actionable.
3. As an active employee, I want to move a task through New, In Progress, Done, and Cancelled, so that its work state is clear.
4. As an active employee, I want to set a Normal or High priority, so that I can sort and filter operational attention without introducing a second status model.
5. As an active employee, I want to give a task an optional day or exact-time deadline, so that planned work is visible without inventing dates for unscheduled work.
6. As an active employee, I want overdue status calculated in the Event timezone, so that everyone sees the same deadline interpretation.
7. As an active employee, I want to complete an overdue task, so that overdue is an honest signal and not an artificial workflow block.
8. As an active employee, I want to reopen or cancel a task with a reason, so that the historical work state remains understandable.
9. As an active employee, I want to see an append-only activity log for creation, assignment, group, priority, deadline, status, delivery, and template actions, so that I can understand what changed and by whom.
10. As an active employee, I want Event and global task lists to show the same persisted task data, so that I can work locally or across Events without duplicate records.
11. As an active employee, I want to filter the global list by Event, Event series, owner, group, status, priority, deadline, overdue state, archive state, and text, so that I can focus on relevant work.
12. As an active employee, I want archived Event tasks hidden from active work by default but retrievable explicitly, so that history remains available without polluting daily work.
13. As an admin, I want to add, rename, sort, and deactivate task groups, so that the organisation can use its own language while preserving historical assignments.
14. As an admin, I want inactive owners or groups retained on existing work but flagged for review, so that deactivation does not falsify history.
15. As an admin, I want a named Event series with versioned task templates, so that annual Events can start from an approved operational standard.
16. As an admin, I want template deadlines relative to Event start or end as well as manual deadlines, so that tasks such as sending bib numbers seven days before an Event reschedule predictably.
17. As an admin, I want a preview and confirmation before moving relative open deadlines after an Event date change, so that manually set and finished dates are never silently changed.
18. As an admin, I want template application to be atomic and idempotent, so that a retried or parallel application creates no duplicate task instances.
19. As an admin, I want templates to create fresh tasks only, so that no completed tasks, comments, risks, blockers, audit data, shipments, or deliveries from a prior Event are copied or changed.
20. As an automation operator, I want a paginated, filtered, read-only Task API secured by a revocable service token, so that n8n can consume current task data without a user session.
21. As an auditor, I want each business mutation and its activity entry written atomically with an immutable audit record, so that failed audit writes cannot leave untraceable changes.
22. As an employee, I want a clear conflict response when another user changed the task first, so that no edit is silently overwritten.
23. As an administrator, I want Events with open tasks blocked from archival and Events with PM history blocked from physical deletion, so that the new history is protected.
24. As a migration operator, I want a verified, access-controlled snapshot of old checkbox tasks before their controlled removal, so that legacy removal is recoverable without corrupting the new model.
25. As a mobile and keyboard user, I want task creation, filtering, status changes, and detail editing without drag-and-drop, so that the workflow remains accessible.

## Implementation Decisions

- Event remains the sole operational project container. Do not introduce a parallel Project aggregate or a ClickUp dependency.
- Add a named Event-series model while preserving existing stable series identifiers. Series own versioned task templates; revisions apply only to future applications.
- The MVP Task workflow is exactly New, In Progress, Done, and Cancelled. Priority is exactly Normal and High. Overdue is a server-calculated display state, never a workflow status and never a completion block.
- A task belongs to one Event, has an optional active User owner, a configurable task group, optional manual or Event-relative deadline, a next step, and an optimistic version.
- Persist Event timezone using an IANA identifier, default Europe/Vienna. Store instant deadlines in UTC and interpret day deadlines in the Event timezone.
- An In Progress task whose owner or group is later deactivated remains In Progress but is visibly marked for reassignment; subsequent substantive edits and completion revalidate active owner, group, and next step.
- Task groups are Admin-managed selection-list-like records. Existing references survive rename or deactivation; used groups are never physically deleted.
- Implement a visible append-only TaskActivity stream separate from the immutable security AuditLog. A business mutation writes TaskActivity and AuditLog in the same Prisma transaction. Comments are a later activity type with their own revision.
- Give Tasks their own expectedVersion and conflict response. The client must show current server state and require an explicit retry; it must not auto-merge.
- Expose one paginated server-side Task read model for UI and n8n. n8n uses a revocable, auditable, read-only PM-scoped service token; no PM email, recipient selection, reminders, claims, or escalation workflow is included.
- Keep delivery status independent from task workflow. Add it in the second increment; Sent is not Delivered, and delivery completion rules never change HardwareIssue or Payout state.
- References may link existing Contact, Communication, HardwareIssue, Payout, and EventFile records. A Task never owns or mutates those records.
- Template application creates new task IDs and new event-internal relations only. It never changes a prior Event or its history. An inactive template owner produces an explicitly confirmed unassigned instance.
- Relative open deadlines are moved only through a version-checked preview and confirmation. Manually dated and terminal tasks are excluded.
- Do not migrate legacy checkbox tasks. Create and verify an access-controlled JSON/CSV snapshot with run metadata and audit evidence, then remove the old records in a controlled cutover.
- New PM history is retained: Events with open Tasks cannot be archived, and Events with PM history cannot be physically deleted until a separate retention decision exists.
- Build the frontend as one Project-Management workspace seam consumed by the Event detail and global Tasks route; keep React, HTTP, Prisma, and browser storage as adapters. Reuse existing cards, tabs, sheets, badges, filters, Event links, and table behavior.
- Defer risks/Red Flags, waiting states, blockers, formal dependencies, free comments, Kanban, and calendar. When introduced, each needs a separate state/API/test contract; overdue must not be repurposed as a Red Flag.

## Testing Decisions

- The highest common seam is the Project-Management workspace/Task API contract. Event-detail and global-list browser tests must exercise that same persisted server model rather than local projections or mock-only stores.
- Use framework-free domain tests for deadline boundaries including DST, relative due-date calculation, simple state transitions, overdue-not-blocking completion, and inactive owner/group validation.
- Use PostgreSQL integration tests for Task version conflicts, atomic TaskActivity plus AuditLog writes, idempotent template application, archive/delete restrictions, read-only n8n scope, and the snapshot/removal cutover.
- Add real browser E2E tests with reload persistence for creation, start, assignment/group/deadline activity entries, completion of overdue work, URL filters, global pagination, template preview/application, rescheduling confirmation, archive/delete protection, 360px layout, and keyboard operation.
- Follow existing Event workspace, Hardware, Payout, AuditLog, and Event-detail browser suites as prior art. Every added feature needs a relevant browser regression as required by AGENTS.md.

## Out of Scope

- A standalone Project app, ClickUp integration or synchronization, and automatic PM email/push notifications.
- Red Flags, risk records, critical priority, waiting status, manual blockers, dependency graphs, comments, Kanban, and calendar in the MVP.
- Event-crossing task dependencies and tasks without an Event.
- Automatic changes to Contact, Communication, HardwareIssue, Payout, or Event data when a Task changes.
- Workday/holiday calendars, custom milestones beyond Event start/end, and Event-specific ACLs.
- Migrating old checkbox tasks into the new Task model.

## Further Notes

The full, evidence-linked design is maintained in `wiki/tasks/project-management-spec-v2.md`. The delivery plan is: MVP task foundation and read API; delivery/dashboard/templates; collaboration features; then optional risk, Kanban, calendar, and scale work. This issue intentionally does not authorize implementation by itself beyond its ready-for-agent triage state.
